newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK BOURSE FOREIGN TRADING DOWN 71 PCT SINCE JAN.
newsitem.headline: TURK BOURSE FOREIGN TRADING DOWN 71 PCT SINCE JAN.

text.p: The volume of foreign trading on the Istanbul stock exchange was down 71 percent in April from January, according to data released by the Turkish bourse.

The data showed that purchases on the accounts of foreign banks, brokerage houses or private investors totalled 17.42 trillion lira in April, while sales on their accounts amounted to 15.57 trillion lira.
In January, foreign purchases totalled 61.42 trillion lira and sales stood at 54.91 trillion.
Market analysts say confidence in the bourse abroad has been dented by a months-old political crisis which has brought the Islamist-led government to the brink of collapse.
The latest of a series of defections from the 11-month-old alliance on Friday left Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's government without an absolute majority in parliament.
The stock exchange chairman said such periodical declines in foreign trading volumes were "quite normal".

"Foreign investors have more alternatives than domestic investors. Hence, at certain times they may prefer to remain liquid by changing their choices. That is quite normal," stock exchange (IMKB) chairman Tuncay Artun told Reuters.
"It is completely natural that foreign investors, who came to the IMKB when there was a crisis in another developing market, should pull out of the IMKB when they became concerned," he said.
He said portoflio investments, which totalled $4.5 billion in January, had fallen to $3.5 billion, according to the latest available data.
Shares rebounded on Friday from the losses of a day earlier, climbing over two percent despite the political impasse.

Foreign trading during both periods focused on companies such as flat steel producer Eregli, financials Akbank, T. Is Bankasi C series and Yapi Kredi, car maker Otosan, utility Cukurova Elektrik and consumer goods maker Arcelik.
